checked: Fixed edges reconstructed from the rooted partition. All subsets of the fixed part checked; all row availability patterns tested with both roots available.
derivation_review: The two roots have seven common and two private neighbours apiece. Triangle-freeness forbids edges within either root neighbourhood. The roots miss the remaining 27 vertices X. An independent eight in X would extend by both roots to ten.

Writing e for the number of A-B edges gives 18+e fixed edges, 81-2e edges to X by the degree sums on the eleven row vertices, and hence 81+e edges inside X. The input lower bound 85 and e<=4 force e=4. This gives the fixed 13-vertex graph used in the truth table.

Exactly five maximal independent sets of the fixed graph occur: C+A, C+B, {u}+B, {w}+A, {u,w}. For any independent I in X, remove from each of these sets the row vertices incident to I. The largest remaining set extends I, and every independent extension is contained in one of the five.

At K=9 the first two families give h_C(I)+h_Q(I)>=|I| for both Q. The one-root inequalities are automatic through size six and require each side union to hit every independent seven. The two-root inequality follows from alpha(X)<=7. All independent I, including non-maximal members, enter this argument.

The four side rows have size six and the seven common rows size seven. Each x must receive exactly 9-deg_X(x) incidences in these eleven rows. Triangles with two core vertices are excluded by row independence; triangles with one core vertex are excluded by disjoint opposite-side unions. Conversely these data build the labelled graph. Repeated common rows count with multiplicity.
Permuting common vertices and swapping the two vertices on a side preserves extensions. Exchanging A and B also exchanges the two roots. Sorting rows only chooses representatives.
premises: The four-core census and Chen's upstream reduction are premises. The graph-to-row review and finite checks concern the completion model.
